The whole calendar shows times in your zone. A shared event stays anchored to the same moment, so each person sees it in their own time.
Event times, day boundaries, and the “now” line all render in this zone — even when you travel and your phone’s clock changes.
A second clock beside yours in the week and day views on the web — handy for a partner in another zone.

Which calendar blocks count as your nights, and whether sleep check-ins move them. Private to you.
When you log a bedtime and wake time, snap that night’s sleep block to match. If there’s no block yet, one is added to your sleep category.
When you log a bedtime and wake time, snap that night’s sleep block to match. With no sleep category set, a new block is added as an inactive event.

When set, only this category’s timed events count as your nights — other inactive blocks (focus time, commutes) stop reading as sleep.
Nights collect sleep between these hours — the start on the evening before, the end on the wake day. Widen it if you sleep past noon or keep unusual hours.

Bring in the nights your watch or sleep app saves to Health Connect: bedtime, wake time and sleep stages show up in Insights → Sleep on the web. For the last 4 nights, your sleep blocks in the calendar move to match (turn off with “Update calendar from check-ins” in Settings → Sleep). Your morning ratings stay yours. How Planr uses your sleep data

Planr reads your sleep sessions from Health Connect: when you went to bed, when you woke up, and the time spent in each sleep stage. It saves one entry per night to your Planr account so the Sleep insights on the web can show them.

This data is private to you: your partner in Planr can't see it, it isn't shared with anyone else, and it is never sent to an AI model. Planr only reads; it never writes to Health Connect.

To stop, choose Disconnect in Planr (account menu → Sleep from Health Connect) or remove Planr's access in Health Connect. Nights already brought in stay in your account until you delete them on the web.
